name: Water

sections.body:
A sietch survives by gathering water, keeping it sealed and carrying it to the people who need it. Colonists and Arrakis livestock have a water need separate from food. A full pantry cannot prevent dehydration when the drinking stores run dry.

Windtraps, condensers and rare wild harvests produce physical water rations. These must be hauled, stored and made accessible, whether the destination is a workshop, a prison room or a caravan bound for another settlement.
sections.title: Water discipline

sections.body:
People begin with 90% hydration. Before heat, exposure and clothing are considered, their water need falls by 70 percentage points per day. They become thirsty below 30% and desperate below 15%; dehydration begins below 30% and can become fatal. Drinking restores the water need and reduces the resulting dehydration.

Keep rations within reach of working and recovering colonists. Supplies that exist only in an inaccessible store cannot help a thirsty pawn.
sections.title: Thirst and dehydration

sections.body:
Desert work consumes water faster than rest in a cool room. The thirst multiplier rises to 1.15 at 20°C, 1.55 at 32°C and 2.1 at 42°C; below freezing it falls to 0.8. Being unroofed adds a further multiplier of 1.12.

A sheltered work area and a cooler room reduce demand before another ration is spent. Plan exposed hauling and spice work with the heat of the day in mind.
sections.title: Heat and shelter

sections.body:
At Normal quality and full condition, a stillsuit reclaims 60% of water loss, a fitted reclamation mask 30%, and a stillsuit headwrap 15%. The mask and headwrap share a slot, so only one can be worn. A stillsuit and mask together reclaim 90% at those conditions.

Workmanship and remaining condition affect each garment separately. Combined retention is capped at 99.9%: even excellent desert equipment leaves a need for drinking water. Check the seals and clothing condition before sending anyone far from shelter.
sections.title: Stillsuits and reclamation seals

sections.body:
Windtraps provide the settlement’s regular supply, drawing moisture from exposed air. Give their intakes open sky and room around nearby walls. A personal condenser is portable emergency equipment for open ground; it stops collecting while carried or enclosed. Rare dew bladders offer a single ration when harvested.

A deep-vent plant condenses a much larger flow where a steam vent can be capped, while also supplying electricity. Such sites are scarce. Cisterns hold sealed rations and protect them from deterioration; colonists still haul and drink those rations as physical supplies.
sections.title: Collectors and cisterns

sections.body:
Fiber cultivation draws from the same reserves as food. A mature four-cell bed of sietch fiber yields 32 coarse fibers and consumes two water rations over a complete growth cycle. Weaving eight fibers produces six Cloth, so a full bed can supply 24 Cloth.

A passive sietch cooler needs 20 Cloth for its pads when built; later cooling uses water. Growing fiber therefore trades planting space and irrigation for useful equipment. Its three growth days describe ideal growing time: darkness, temperature, water shortages and labor can extend the calendar. Wild windcup is a small supplementary source.
sections.title: The water cost of cloth

sections.body:
Powered sietch cultivation provides fertile troughs for reclaimed Arrakis crops. Each trough has 2.8 fertility, a 70 W pump and an initially empty two-ration reserve. Water is charged as plants grow, so faster growth spends water sooner without reducing the cost of a complete harvest. Power failures can kill the crop. Cultivation lights draw 2,900 W while scheduled on and rest with the plants.

Ornamental windcup uses a separate planter with an initially empty one-ration reserve. Establishing the plant consumes half a ration; once mature, it has no further growth-based water charge. It yields no food, fiber or medicine.
sections.title: Irrigation under a roof

sections.body:
Traders and guests arrive with their own finite drinking supply, sized for their visit and desert equipment. They drink from carried rations rather than drawing freely from the colony’s cisterns. When the group cannot cover the remaining visit and an exit reserve, it prepares to leave while its members can still walk.

A meeting spot on genuine rock gives visitors a safer place to wait. It does not make the route across open sand safe.
sections.title: Guests and passing caravans

sections.body:
Pack drinking water as well as food. Human travelers and supported kulon, desert mice and sand terrapins consume physical water rations from caravan inventories. Each thirsty member uses one ration, looking first in its own inventory and then in shared supplies. Empty packs provide no replacement.

Stillsuit retention and species demand still matter. Off-map travel currently uses baseline thirst conditions rather than the map’s heat and roof exposure multipliers, so caravan demand does not reproduce every local weather condition.
sections.title: Provisioning a caravan

sections.body:
Prisoners need drinking water separately from their meals. With Warden work enabled, a colonist can carry an existing ration to a thirsty captive in a valid prison room, or assist one who cannot drink unaided. A downed captive must first be placed in a bed.

A mobile captive can drink accessible water placed in the same prison room, subject to its water-access rules. The prison-cell food filter supplies no water by itself. Stock rations separately and keep the room reachable for wardens.
sections.title: Water for captives

sections.body:
A deathstill returns two sealed water rations from an eligible fresh humanlike corpse. Reclamation happens once and leaves desiccated remains for burial. Animal bodies, rotten bodies and previously drained remains provide no further water.

The 250 W sietch funerary chamber has separate disposal bills for drained remains and other ineligible organic bodies. Fresh reclaimable human bodies are protected. New bills require explicit permission before colonists or other non-hostiles are included; older bills keep their saved permissions. Remove equipment you wish to keep before disposal, which destroys the remaining contents and produces nothing. Thermal disposal is a practical adaptation for this mod rather than a Fremen religious rite.
sections.title: Reclamation and the dead

summary: Water sustains every journey, harvest and household on Arrakis. Collectors replenish the stores; sealed clothing and sheltered rooms make those stores last.
